        c[f_function(x) ^ f_function(x ^ d)] += 1
    top = c.most_common(3)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Chosen-plaintext attack recovering key[5] of the FEAL-like cipher.

Cipher structure (see feal.py).  For a 64-bit plaintext (L0, R0):

    A = L0 ^ key[0]
    B = R0 ^ key[1] ^ A
    3 Feistel rounds with keys key[2], key[3], key[4]
    final Feistel round with key[5]
    final mix,  CT_hi = right, CT_lo = left

Let (Q, R3) be the (left, right) halves entering the final round, with
Q the input to the F-function there.  Then

    CT_hi = R3 ^ F(Q ^ key[5])
    CT_lo = R3 ^ Q ^ F(Q ^ key[5])      (after the final left ^= right)

so

    Q  = CT_hi ^ CT_lo                  (known from the ciphertext alone!)
    R3 = CT_hi ^ F(Q ^ key[5])          (known once key[5] is guessed)

Differential characteristic of F (probability 1):
    F(x) ^ F(x ^ 0x00008080) == 0x00000002   for every x.
Why: in G(a,b,x)=rotl2(a+b+x) a lone 0x80 difference on one input changes
the sum by exactly 0x80 (a single carry-free bit flip), and
rotl2(0x80) = 0x02.  In F, input diff 0x00008080 puts 0x80 in bytes x0 and
x1: the y2 and y1 sub-functions see (x1^x0) unchanged, y3 sees x3 unchanged
and y2 unchanged, and y0 = G(x0, y1, 1) sees a lone 0x80 -> flips by 0x02.

Chosen pair: L0_1 ^ L0_2 = R0_1 ^ R0_2 = 0x00008080.
Then A1^A2 = 0x00008080 (key[0] cancels) and B1^B2 = 0 (key[1] cancels).
Inside the 3-round function:
    key[2] round: F input diff 0            -> diff 0
    key[3] round: F input diff 0x00008080   -> diff 0x00000002 (prob 1)
    key[4] round: (irrelevant for R3)
and R3 = B ^ F(A ^ F(B^key[2]) ^ key[3]), so
    R3_1 ^ R3_2 = 0 ^ 0x00000002 = 0x00000002   with certainty.

Hence, for the true key[5]:
    F(Q1 ^ k5) ^ F(Q2 ^ k5) == CT_hi1 ^ CT_hi2 ^ 0x00000002.

A wrong k5 satisfies this with probability ~2^-32 per pair.

Keyspace: key[i] = (seed[i] * 1234567) mod 2^32 with a 16-bit seed, so only
2^16 values of key[5] are possible.  We test all of them against a handful
of chosen pairs; the true key is the unique survivor.
